title: Thermal equilibrium
body: Thermal equilibrium is the condition in which no net energy is transferred by thermal processes between two systems in thermal contact with each other.
ced_evidence: 9.3.A.4: "Thermal equilibrium results when no net energy is transferred by thermal processes between two systems in thermal contact with each other."

title: First law of thermodynamics
caution: The CED states the first law as conservation of energy for a closed system: the change in internal energy is the sum of energy transferred by heating (or cooling) and work done on the system. In \Delta U = Q + W, W is work done ON the system. Work done by the gas on its surroundings makes W negative. For an isolated system, the total energy is constant.
ced_evidence: 9.4.B.1.ii: "the change in internal energy is the sum of energy transferred to or from the system by heating, or work done on the system"

title: Pressure–volume (PV) diagram
body: A graph of pressure versus volume that represents a thermodynamic process, where the area under the curve gives the absolute value of the work done on or by the gas.

items.label: Area under the curve
items.meaning: Absolute value of the work done on the gas when it expands or compresses

items.label: Isotherm
items.meaning: A line of constant temperature on the PV diagram

items.label: Adiabatic process
items.meaning: No energy transferred to or from the system through thermal processes

caution: Area under the curve gives only the absolute value of the work. Determine the sign of W from whether the gas is compressed (work done on the gas, W > 0) or expanded (W < 0).
ced_evidence: 9.4.B.2: "Pressure-volume graphs (also known as PV diagrams) are representations used to represent thermodynamic processes"; 9.4.B.2.ii: "equal to the area underneath the curve of a plot of pressure vs. volume"
